changelog.entry: New: up to three named forests on one browser, such as "Ranger practice". Open the save pill (top right), then Forest, to start a new one, rename it, switch between them or delete one. Each forest keeps its own save, difficulty, grid size and tree choice, and switching saves the one you are in first. The first one, My forest, simply keeps the progress you already have. Signed-in players keep their three account slots instead.

New: when you finish a level there is now a Next level button beside Leave level. It starts the following level straight away (and says why it is greyed out if that level is still locked); Leave level still takes you back to free play on the same forest. Changed: the Badge frame and Palette pickers no longer sit above the map. On Desktop they are in a Forest Rank and badge frame window (Menu, Records), which gives the map back its room; on the Classic page they sit under the map and the stats.

Fixed: achievements no longer vanish when you start a new level. Once you have earned one, it stays earned for the whole game, and the achievements panel now shows the whole game's list with everything you have earned. Saves from before this fix bring back whatever they had listed as earned.

Keyboard and screen-reader play: selecting a plot (Enter, Space or a click) now tells the screen-reader live region which plot it is, what state it is in and which keys act on it, and C, K or R on a plot where they cannot work now say why (already bare, still replanting, the Heart Tree is never felled, only a bare plot can be replanted) instead of staying silent. A repeated message is spoken again. The gold cursor ring on the plot the arrow keys are on, and the C (clear), K (clear-cut) and R (replant) hotkeys, are unchanged and listed in the ? overlay. The phone action dock also fits again: its buttons scroll sideways and the tree picker and plot note fold behind the ... button.

New: Expedition mode (the Expedition button, or the Menu on Desktop). A separate 12-season run (about 8 minutes at normal speed, 2 at 4x) on a map decided by a shareable seed such as CANOPY-K7F2Q. The seed only decides the map: 6 rich-soil plots (marked with an up triangle, +25% growth), 6 thin-soil plots (a down triangle, -20%) and 4 plots that start bare. You get 3 upgrade points at the start and one more every season, and spend them in a skill tree with three branches (Growth, Soil and recovery, Trade and tending). The whole tree costs more than you can earn, so the build is your choice, and taking an upgrade back is free. Nothing is random, nothing is lost and there is no way to fail: after season 12 you get a score (standing value plus income) and your best per seed is kept on this device. Leave Expedition returns to normal play on the same forest, and normal saves are unchanged. Seed Vault perks rest during an Expedition so runs stay comparable. Two new achievements: Twelve Seasons and Two Maps.

New: Clear-cut. Select a standing plot and press Clear-cut (or K) to bank 20% more income than a plain Clear. The price is a visible soil dip: the plot's growth drops by up to 30 points and heals in a straight line over about three seasons (120 ticks), whether the plot is bare, replanting or growing again. It carries a down-arrow mark, its tooltip and the soil readout say how long is left, and Undo takes it back. There are no dice. Clear-cuts count toward the Harvester playstyle badge, which now shows how many of your clears were clear-cuts, and there are two new achievements, Quick Payout and Harvester.

New: the legacy bonus is now a small chip whose tooltip names where it came from (your last forest's standing value) and how close it is to the +25% cap. If the forest kept growing while the tab was hidden you get a 'While you were away' chip saying what changed. Plots can now carry a short note (up to 20 characters): type it in the Plot note box under the plot readout, or right-click or long-press a plot to jump to the box; a noted plot shows a dot and its note in the tooltip. On a slow device or a busy tab the game now pauses its decorative effects (wildlife flutter, value pops, leaf bursts) and shows a small 'Performance mode' note until the game is steady again; nothing about the game itself changes. On a phone, long-pressing a plot opens a bottom sheet with large Clear, Replant, Adopt and Edit note buttons for that plot; the desktop layout is unchanged. Every plot now shows a small drawn tree, sapling or stump that follows the season (you can switch these off in Settings).

The Session Summary has a Request history table: every community request you answered, your choice, and how that plot's value has changed since, sortable and filterable. The Session Summary also has Lifetime statistics: sessions finished, plots cleared and replanted, time in the forest and your average standing value by difficulty, kept on this device. The Session Summary has a Download forest card button: a 1200 by 630 picture of your final grid with your playstyle badge and three headline numbers, drawn in code, each plot also marked with a letter so it reads without colour. A new opt-in setting, Coach hints, adds short notes to the Session Summary that read your forest (a plot cleared three times, soil below 60%, bare plots with nothing replanted, low community relations); they never block play and can be dismissed. The Session Summary has a Timeline chart: a larger graph of standing value, biodiversity or community relations over the recent ticks, with season bands, hover values on every point and shaped markers for each clear, replant, specialist choice and answered request (a text list of the events sits underneath). My Forests keeps a record of each forest you finish (the latest twelve, on this device): pick any two in the Session Summary to compare their numbers and their three trend graphs side by side. The Session Summary also has a Forest replay: drag the slider to watch the grid change through the session, plots clearing, replanting and recovering in sequence (letters as well as colours, so a screenshot reads in greyscale). The Compare with other players button now also compares your standing forest value with other players (it needs the next backend update to show the new line).

A new Scenario picker starts you in a ready-made forest: Clear-cut Valley (60% of plots bare), Fragmented Farmland (a checkerboard) or Old-Growth Remnant (only one intact core). Each scenario keeps its own best standing value. A Forest Lab (sandbox) in the Session Summary has four dials from half to double: soil damage per clear, growth over time, request frequency and season strength. Dials are staged until you press Apply, which starts a new forest; a sandbox forest is clearly marked and never counts toward personal bests, lifetime statistics, the legacy bonus, My Forests, scenario bests or Forest Rank. You can save a set of dials as a named variant (up to six) and stage it again later.

Community clear requests now have a third answer, Counter-offer: replant the nearest bare plots instead (up to two), or, if none are bare, harvest half of the plot's value and keep it standing. The button's tooltip previews the exact numbers. Community requests now come from recurring named people with a small drawn portrait and a mood: the mayor (housing), a farmer, the timber foreman, the carbon broker (offers) and the restoration ranger (grants). Granting, countering and accepting offers builds trust; a decline just leaves them disappointed and never costs trust. At trust 5 a person becomes an ally and at 8 a champion, and each stretches the time between requests (10% and 20%, at most 50% in all). A Community faces section in the Session Summary lists who you have met.

A long-term Forest Rank (Sapling Warden up to Grove Keeper) grows with your lifetime standing value, seasons survived and each playstyle badge type you earn; it only unlocks cosmetic badge frames (told apart by edge style) and palettes under the achievements, never gameplay. The achievements panel is now a grove wall: cards tile like the plot grid, each with a wildlife icon, earned ones lit and marked Earned, locked ones a dim silhouette marked Locked with their progress line kept.

A Survey button pauses time so you can plan: Clear, Replant and a decline of the current request are queued instead of happening, a panel shows what the plan would do (income, standing value given up, the gap to the left-standing forest, soil quality), and Commit runs the whole plan and lets time run again. Cancel throws the plan away.

Replanting now lets you choose the tree: Pioneer pine (recovers in half the time, lower value), Hardwood oak (twice the wait, more value and wildlife) or an Orchard (steady income, no wildlife), or the standard seedling. A forest standing with a mix of species grows 5% faster per extra species. Each chosen species has its own shape mark on the tile and its own Almanac entry. Blight: five or more connected plots of one chosen tree build up blight; after 40 ticks you get a warning, and from 60 ticks it kills the least valuable plot back to bare every 10 ticks (no soil damage) until the patch is broken up. Tend any plot in the patch to reset it, or plant a different species in the middle. It is on by default and can be switched off in Settings; standard seedlings never count. Neighbour synergy: a mature plot grows 4% faster for each mature plot sharing an edge with it (up to 16%), shown by a small +link mark and a tooltip line, and a bare plot next to a mature one recovers 20% faster when replanted. Solid blocks pay, checkerboards do not, and a protected core with a cleared edge replants quickly. The +link marks can be hidden in Settings (the bonus stays).

New difficulty option, Wildfire season (opt-in). In summer and some autumns smoke appears over a standing plot three ticks before a spark catches there. A burning plot sets its standing neighbours alight and burns out to bare after four ticks, losing its value but not harming the soil. Bare and replanting plots are firebreaks, so you can clear a plot on purpose to save a mature cluster, or select a burning or smoking plot and press Dampen (a short cooldown applies, and the plot stays safe for a while). The Heart Tree never burns. Fire is marked with a flame glyph and a solid outline, smoke with a dotted outline.

The Wetland Forest now has tides. Every six ticks the tide turns and the two halves of the wetland swap between under water (a wave mark and a dashed lower edge) and dry. A dry bare plot takes a normal seedling; a flooded bare plot can only take a new tree, the mangrove, which recovers fast and is not harmed by the big flood. Mangrove stands bring tidal wildlife into the Almanac (a heron from three standing mangroves, a crab once one is mature).

New optional Carbon market in the Session Summary. Standing plots earn carbon credits every tick; the price moves on a known cycle (the chart shows the recent price and the next few ticks dotted, with a trend word), so selling is a matter of timing, not luck. Selling pays now but slows the forest's growth for a few ticks, longer for bigger sales, so it only pays when the price is high. Accepting the carbon broker's offers also gifts credits. Credits can sit unsold as long as you like.

New opt-in daily community plot. Tick Water the community plot in Settings and a small share of your forest's growth (more when more of your forest is standing) is added to one anonymous shared total, shown in the Session Summary with today's total and the best day. Your own contribution today can also go on an opt-in daily, weekly and all-time board (sign in and tick the board's box). Nothing is sent unless you turn it on, and sandbox forests never contribute.

New Custom layouts section in the Session Summary: pick Island, Ring, Plus or River split (or toggle cells yourself) to decide which cells of the grid are plots and which are open ground, then Apply to start a new forest on that shape. Open ground never grows, cannot be selected and is left out of every count. Save up to six named layouts, each with its own best standing value. A layout forest has no scenario, challenge or level, does not set the standard personal best or averages, and is kept out of the community comparison.

New difficulty option, Rival logging company (opt-in). Halloran Timber Co. bids on a standing plot on the edge of the grid: it is flagged ten ticks ahead, then becomes a mining claim (bare, cannot be replanted) for 40 ticks before Halloran leaves it free again. You can lock any plot with a conservation easement, which costs a share of that plot's value from your income and keeps it safe for good, or pay to buy a claim out early. Bids come faster as the session goes on, down to a floor. Nothing is lost for good: a claimed plot always comes back.

New: the Session Summary has a Copy result button that copies one line, such as Canopy, 41.2 standing forest value, with your harvested income, biodiversity and plots still standing. Every achievement you have earned now has a Share button that copies a line you can paste anywhere, with the share of players who have it when that figure is available. The How to Play and Info panels link to the new Credits page. New: a Pause, 1x, 2x and 4x control sits under the toolbar (Space pauses or resumes, [ and ] change the speed). Faster only means the game ticks more often, never that anything is skipped, and nothing at all happens while it is paused. New: a setting, on by default, pauses the game while this browser tab is hidden and tells you when you come back; switch it off in Settings if you want it to keep running in the background. New: a Levels screen (the Levels button, or the Menu on Desktop) with 15 levels. Every fifth one is a mode or a new mechanic: Poacher Patrol (click the plot, or press P, before a poacher strikes), Storm Front (replant the gaps before each front sweeps two rows) and The Spirit's Walk (a forest spirit sets six small tasks and narrates them); the four challenge runs are levels too. Your best result for each level is kept. New: the Seed Vault, a skill tree you spend seed points in (1 point for each level completed, forest tier reached and every 4 achievements): growth and soil perks, plus idle ranger crews that tend, catch seedlings and replant for you. Perks rest during challenge runs. In Settings, Level effects turns off the modes' animations.

New: four challenge runs (Pacifist, Scorched Start, Sprint, No-Highland) each with a badge and a fastest-finish record; a Ranger contracts board with three open contracts, income rewards, ranks and ten collectable stamps; a forecast line showing the next two seasons and the next rain or drought; a Request pace choice (relaxed, normal, frequent); a two-line plot card with age, biodiversity rate and clear count; C and R keys to clear or replant the selected plot, a thicker gold cursor ring and a screen-reader announcer; and in Settings, high-contrast plots (B / G / M / R letters and bold borders), a soil quality overlay and a number format choice. Fixes from player reports: on a phone the action buttons now sit in one compact row at the bottom (a ... button unfolds the tend hint and forest name) so the forest grid is no longer buried under pinned panels; the arrow keys move between plots again and keep their place from one second to the next; Reset Session now opens a clear Cancel / Reset session dialog (Esc cancels) instead of needing a quick second press; and on the Desktop layout the side column fits without scrolling, with the forest summary, the forest picture and Name your forest moved into the Menu.

Canopy now has a Desktop layout for wide windows with a mouse: the forest grid fills the window, the actions for the selected plot and any community request sit beside it, income, standing value, biodiversity and relations are chips along the top, and the Almanac, achievements, session summary, settings and the Highland and Wetland regions open as windows (press Esc for the menu). Same saves as the Classic layout, and you can switch from the menu or the opening screen.

Canopy gamified batch: golden seedlings to catch (or press G), a Tend action (T) with a cooldown, a hidden Heart Tree for the curious, name your forest and nickname an adopted plot, a short Undo after Clear (not in Forest ranger), rare wildlife with conditions (a ghost stag at late-autumn dusk, a wary fox), forest tiers (Seedling, Grove, Woodland, Old-Growth) with three new achievements, rain and drought on the season indicator, chain-bloom leaf ripples, a Forest Almanac, and a Perfect Season flame streak. Light theme polish: Canopy now has a proper light look. The readouts, plot tile edges, selection and flood outlines, info buttons, switch lights and session graphs were re-coloured so they stay readable on a light page, and the Light/Dark control moved from a floating pill into the Settings panel. The dark theme looks exactly as before and no save or game number changed. In the real world: a collapsible note beside the forest pairs what you just did with one sourced real example. Clearing shows global forest-loss figures, replanting the Atlantic Forest Restoration Pact, wildlife how regrown forest recovers, a mature plot forest carbon sinks, and a community request Nepal's community forestry or Africa's Great Green Wall. Each names its source and links to it, and it never changes your forest or save (W2).

Story mode: the Wren Hollow story. A short chapter is added to a collapsible Story panel for each achievement you earn, from the first cut to a closed canopy. It is optional, follows the existing Story on/off pill, and never changes your save (W1). Wetland Forest: a third region unlocked at 5000 standing forest value. It grows 25% faster than the main forest, but a flood sweeps it every 50 ticks — young plots lose 30% of their value, mature ones 10%, replanting plots get silted back — with a 10-tick warning so you can harvest ahead of the water (B1). Example playthrough: a narrated, worked-out example of a strong preserve/clear balance, with every number calculated from the game's own settings (B29).

Achievement cards now show "Earned by N% of players" once enough real save data exists for that achievement (site-wide goal, Z1/Z27b). Added a keyboard-shortcuts help overlay: press ? to see it, Esc to close it or whichever panel is open (site-wide goal, Z4).

Settings panel: added a "Reset to Default" button that resets text size and reduce-motion back to their defaults in one click (site-wide goal, folded from A26). Session Summary is now print-friendly: printing the page (e.g. Ctrl/Cmd+P) while it's open hides the site chrome and renders the summary in clean dark-on-white, instead of the site's usual dark theme and UI. Highland Grove now has its own distinct rates: soil degrades 50% faster per clear and standing value compounds 25% slower than the main forest, reflecting a harsher high-altitude ecosystem. Round-2 pass, remaining items: reforestation partner (faster replant recovery for a permanent value share), a legacy forest bonus carried into the next session from the last one's standing value, a seasonal growth cycle, and the shared personal-best badge flash (also rolled out to Tide and Thaw).

Round-2 pass: Small 4x4 grid, Forest ranger difficulty, forest history + wildlife log, playstyle badge, report-card graphs, veteran and adopted plots, specialist plots, replanting grants, Highland unlock progress bar, biodiversity rate, and an opt-in community comparison. Onboarding-tooltip coverage audit completed — legend and stakeholder info-icons plus per-plot tooltips already cover every non-obvious mechanic, no gap found.
Settings panel added: text size (A-/A/A+) and a reduce-motion toggle, both persisted per-browser.
Space theme visual pass: starfield background, glass panels, gradient buttons, gradient-glow title.
Code-quality audit: fixed a create_proxy memory leak in the plot-grid render loop and a stale stakeholder-request bug that could hand out a free relations bonus.
Pass 3 (fun/teaching balance): re-paced stakeholder tension and the biodiversity payoff closer together to close an early idle stretch.
Info Page added with curated real-world sources on deforestation and carbon sinks. Pass 2: biodiversity sub-meter (wildlife icons on mature plots) and stakeholder-tension decision events.
Pass 1: continuous plot-maturity color gradient, recovery-milestone flash, and a real-world context blurb.
All 7 milestones complete: plot grid, passive value accrual, clearing + soil degradation, replant recovery, comparison scoring, feedback prompt, visual pass + hub integration.
